source.title: On Model and Data Scaling for Skeleton-based Self-Supervised Gait Recognition
source.authors: Adrian Cosma; Andy Catruna; Emilian Radoi

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Conceptually tests scaling in a different domain and with downstream recognition accuracy rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The study measures power-law trends in skeleton-based gait recognition, not language-model loss. It reports no test of language-model loss extrapolation or of a compute-optimal parameter/token split. The plotted scaling results in Figures 3–10 are not numerically extractable from the supplied text; rows for those results record only the authors’ explicit textual descriptions. Cited scaling-law results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws of zero-shot downstream accuracy to model size and pretraining-data size for self-supervised skeleton-based gait transformers. It also checks held-out larger runs against the fitted trends. That is a new modality and regime with its own scaling results, so it bears on V5. It does not measure language-model loss, so V1–V4 and V6 (as stated for language models) are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that power-law trends in downstream zero-shot accuracy hold for self-supervised gait recognition and let performance be predicted from smaller models and data. They also conclude that higher-quality data improves performance and steepens data scaling, and that GaitPTv2 scales better with data than GaitFormer because it uses more compute per sequence. They add that their models are likely undertrained.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales self-supervised skeleton-based gait models and measures downstream recognition accuracy, not language-model pretraining cross-entropy. It uses a different modality, objective, dataset, and outcome measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Fitted exponents vary across dataset sizes, model sizes, controlled versus in-the-wild scenarios, and data-quality selection. The authors also report possible saturation at larger dataset sizes and different data-scaling behavior between GaitPTv2 and GaitFormer.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched compute, the hierarchical GaitPTv2 scales better with data than the flat GaitFormer, attributed to more compute per sequence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture (hierarchical vs flat tokenisation) changes the data-scaling slope at fixed compute budgets.

record.problems: The pretraining dataset is private. Scaling curves are largely presented in figures without extractable numerical point values in the supplied text. The paper reports possible saturation and dataset noise at large data scales; models may also be undertrained. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the scaling exponents.
record.rows_left_out: No reported numerical scaling exponents were omitted. Figures 8–10 discuss iso-accuracy, compute efficiency, and dollar-cost trends but do not provide a result on the language-model versions or a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation; plotted numerical values are not extractable from the supplied text.

untested.parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss; this study measures contrastive-gait downstream accuracy, not loss.
Extrapolation for language models, and over orders of magnitude. The gait extrapolation covers only one or two held-out points.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. IsoFLOP curves are shown, but no optimal-allocation law is derived.
The Deep & Thin and Shallow & Wide variants are never compared at fixed parameter count.
Scaling of loss (rather than accuracy) in this domain, ranges beyond about 2 orders of magnitude, training to saturation (fixed 25 epochs), and other modalities.
Language-model downstream predictability, and any relation of downstream accuracy to pretraining loss.
Language-model fitting-choice dependence and disagreement between published laws.

missing.what: Dollar-cost scaling trend with a held-out validation point. The text says the fitted line accurately estimates downstream accuracy, but gives no numbers.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. The metric is accuracy, fitted as P = N^α + E via log-log regression, not loss. No fit-quality or uncertainty numbers are reported. Models are trained for a fixed 25 epochs and are likely undertrained, by the authors' own account. The pretraining dataset is private.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger language-model runs from smaller runs.
The loss-minimizing parameter/token allocation and its growth with compute; the study compares accuracy at compute budgets but does not derive this allocation law.
Architecture effects on language-model loss at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities and regimes beyond skeleton-based self-supervised gait pretraining and zero-shot downstream gait accuracy.
Downstream performance beyond the four gait benchmarks and settings studied; no relationship to pretraining loss is tested.
Whether published language-model laws disagree; dependence on parameter-counting conventions, training schedules, fitting methods, and compute-optimal allocation.
